group.status: PB1 neutral vectors; data only; validated without loading either stack

given: maxFrameBytes is declared as 65536
when: The length prefix declares a larger body
then: The frame is refused on the prefix alone, before the body is read
No partial request effect begins

given: maxNestingDepth is declared as 32
when: A frame nests arrays or maps beyond that depth
then: Decoding stops at the bound rather than recursing
No partial request effect begins

given: Replay protection and its binding-scoped window are declared
Request r1 was accepted inside the window
when: Request r1 is received again inside the window
then: The repeat is refused
The effect is not repeated

given: maxConcurrentRequests is 1 and the binding is in state 'active'
when: A second request arrives before the first outcome
then: The second request is refused, because version 0.1 promises no ordering or concurrency

given: An outcome for request r1 was accepted and the binding returned to 'ready'
when: A second outcome for r1 arrives
then: The duplicate is refused rather than overwriting the first
No second effect is attributed

given: An established, ready binding with no outstanding request
when: The host withdraws and then terminates
then: Both transitions are legal
No new request is accepted after withdrawal
The terminal state releases no resource by implication

given: The Binding Plan is frozen and immutable for this scope
when: A second establish frame arrives on the same binding
then: The frame is refused, because a changed fact requires a new binding scope rather than renegotiation in place

given: ioTimeoutMilliseconds is declared as 10000
A request was sent
when: No valid outcome arrives within the declared bound
then: The observation is a timeout, not a fabricated success
The failure domain is recorded relative to this observer

expected.effectCountNotAsserted: A timeout says nothing about whether the peer performed the effect before the bound elapsed. Asserting zero here would fabricate knowledge this endpoint does not have.

given: A length prefix declared a body of n bytes
when: The stream ends before n bytes arrive
then: The partial frame is discarded
The observation records interruption rather than a malformed message

expected.effectCountNotAsserted: The partial frame cannot be attributed to a request, so whether a provider effect occurred is not observable here.

given: A valid request carries channel c1, request r1, and optional execution e1
when: The peer returns a terminal successful Outcome echoing every carried identity
then: The Outcome is accepted
The host records a distinct host-native Execution identity

given: A valid request carries request r1
when: The claimed Outcome carries request r2
then: The Outcome is not accepted
The failure is attributed to the observing endpoint

expected.effectCountNotAsserted: The outcome claims a request this host never sent, so no effect can be attributed to it from this endpoint.

given: An outcome envelope requires a requestId
when: The field is absent
then: The envelope is rejected rather than matched to the single outstanding request by position

expected.effectCountNotAsserted: Without a correlation identity the frame cannot be attributed to a request, so no effect count is attributable.

given: A structurally valid envelope
when: Its kind or body discriminator is outside the declared envelope kinds
then: The envelope is rejected
An unknown kind is never treated as a no-op

expected.effectCountNotAsserted: An unrecognized kind carries no attributable request, so no effect count is attributable.

given: A compatible established contract
when: A request names an Operation outside that contract
then: The request is refused
No provider effect begins

given: An authorized request reaches the provider
when: The domain Operation reports structured failure details in its declared detail Shape
then: A failed Outcome crosses and the result is absent
The failure is not a protocol or process failure
No exception is transported

given: Two realizations use different local code strings for an unsupported contract
when: Each adapter reports the portable observation
then: Both observations carry the same portable category
Local code strings remain non-normative data

given: The endpoint cannot continue protocol processing
when: Its local implementation raises a runtime-specific failure
then: The portable category is internal-protocol-failure
No exception, stack trace, or runtime type crosses

expected.effectCountNotAsserted: The endpoint lost the ability to continue protocol processing, so it cannot determine whether a provider effect had already occurred.

given: A request was sent and no valid Outcome was received
when: The peer process terminates
then: The observation is peer-terminated
Retry and fallback facts are explicit
Success is never fabricated

expected.effectCountNotAsserted: The peer may have performed the effect before terminating. C4 requires that success is never fabricated; it does not license fabricating a zero effect count either.

given: No valid semantic Outcome is available
when: The independent stack adapter classifies the local observation
then: It selects exactly one declared process category
Unknown retains the reason narrower attribution was impossible
Success is never fabricated

expected.effectCountNotAsserted: The seven categories differ in whether an effect occurred; a single count across all of them would be wrong for some.

given: Equivalent failures are observed at different Channel boundaries
when: Each adapter records the failure relative to its observer
then: It selects exactly one declared failure domain
No domain value claims global topology

expected.effectCountNotAsserted: The vector varies the observer, not the effect; the count is not what it fixes.
